question_text: A 12-year-old boy and his mother are brought to the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident. The boy was an unrestrained passenger in a head-on collision and was ejected from the front seat. The patient's mother was the driver and she is currently being resuscitated. Neither the child nor the mother are conscious; however, it is documented that the family are all Jehovah's witnesses and would not want a transfusion in an acute situation. The husband/father arrives to the trauma bay and confirms this wish that everyone in the family would not want a transfusion in accordance with their beliefs. The father is confirmed as the official healthcare proxy. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

        ### Question

The boy was an unrestrained passenger in a head-on collision and was ejected from the front seat. The patient's mother was the driver and she is currently being resuscitated. The husband/father arrives to the trauma bay and confirms this wish that everyone in the family would not want a transfusion in accordance with their beliefs. The father is confirmed as the official healthcare proxy. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

opb. Do not transfuse the boy and transfuse the mother
opc. Do not transfuse the boy or the mother
opd. Do not transfuse the mother and transfuse the boy
ope. Transfuse the boy and mother
